e705_gated_bypass.question: does a closed-form quadratic predictor, or a Pile-fitted one, close the gated models' gap in the bypass's transfer, and is the field itself stable across domains?
G1: the quadratic bypass (256 random bilinear features) recovers 0.1 more of the zeroing cost than the linear one on wikitext
G1b: the quadratic bypass reaches 0.9 of the oracle sixteen
G2: the Pile-fitted linear bypass keeps 0.7 of its in-domain recovery out of domain
G2b: the wikitext-fitted linear bypass does (e702's result restated per model)
G3: the Pile-fitted quadratic bypass recovers at least 0.6 out of domain
G4: the field's sixteen directions found on wikitext and on the Pile overlap by more than 0.7
G5: out of domain the quadratic bypass beats the linear one by 0.1

e706_strong_field.question: does a strong-write field beside the weak one carry the rest of a pruned neuron's error?
H1: the strong field alone halves the sixteen-wire ratio at the firings
H2: weak and strong together beat the weak field alone by 0.1
H3: both fields with the attention units bring the ratio under 0.25
H5: both fields beat a random subspace of their dimension by 0.2
H6: both fields halve the all-position ratio

e701_late.question: when does OLMo-1B's brake cross -0.5: checkpoints 32000 to 512000 at blocks 8 and 12
L1: the brake is under -0.5 by step 128000 (nine percent of training) at both blocks
L2: it deepens monotonically from 32000 to the final model (Spearman under -0.8)
